newsitem.title: CANADA: Blue chips lead year-end Toronto market rally.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips lead year-end Toronto market rally.

text.p: The champagne corks popped early on Monday as investors celebrated the onset of 1997, luring many investors into Canadian large-capitalization shares and helping the Toronto market to a solid rally.
Canadian blue chips were also energized by the year-end portfolio shuffle by fund managers and falling bond rates.
"They keep saying it's portfolio stuff but I think people are still buying the brand names and there is still a great deal of optimism," said Fred Ketchen, senior vice-president of ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
"I think it's people getting into the market before the January and February (retirement fund investment) rush comes along," Ketchen said.
Such large-cap issues as Potash Corp of Saskatchewan Inc, Imperial Oil Ltd, Thomson Corp and Bank of Nova Scotia shot higher in relatively brisk midafternoon trade on Monday.
Potash Corp was up 2.00 at 115.00 while Imperial added 2.00 to 64.75. Media and travel giant Thomson rose 1.65 to 30.50 and ScotiaBank appreciated 1.10 to 46.75.
The TSE 300 Composite Index was up 58.09, or nearly one percent, at 5960.70 in midafternoon trade on Monday.

Several traders attributed the large-cap leap to traditional year-end "window-dressing" or portfolio shuffling by fund managers. But others put the gains down to falling rates and buying by investors with a rosy view of next year.
All but one of Toronto's 14 subsectors were higher at midafternoon.
Falling interest rates in the United States and Canada over the past few sessions pumped up rate-sensitive sectors such as real estate, conglomerates and financial services.
"Usually, you get a beginning of the year rally and I think you are just seeing people get a jump on the pack here," said Rolie Bradley, a trader at Maison Placements Canada.
The communications and media group got a boost both from the climb in Thomson shares and from a report by brokerage Merrill Lynch which initiated coverage on several communications shares.
Merrill started coverage on Rogers Communications Inc with a near-term neutral rating and a long-term accumulate. Rogers shares climbed to 9.95 before settling back to trade 0.20 higher at 9.90.

Merrill started Shaw Communications and Groupe Videotron, both of them with a near and long-term accumulate rating. Shaw edged up 0.05 to 7.75 while Videotron climbed 0.30 to 10.80. It close December 24 at 10.50.
